userStories.title: Run the feature workflow on the step graph
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Run the existing feature workflow on FEATURE_GRAPH through runStepGraph without changing valid-run behavior.

**Motivation** — Until the workflow runs on the graph, the engine is unproven against real behaviour and the transitions stay buried in step code that nothing else can reuse.

**Approach**

### Approach

A mechanical port, not a redesign. Every step function keeps its body: the same seam calls, ledger writes, artifacts and `startStep` log lines on stage `workflow`, in the same order. Three things change in each step function:

1. It no longer puts `step` in its patch. `step` is an engine key (`ENGINE_KEYS`), and the engine rejects a patch that names it.
2. Where it chose between destinations, it returns an exit label instead (table below). The graph's transitions map the label to the next node.
3. It returns `{ patch, exit? }` (`StepResult<WorkflowFeatureRecord>`) instead of a bare patch.

The loop's own policies move to the engine, which already reproduces them (G1 § Runner order): abort before `sink.step`, `sink.step` before the cost stop, the cost stop only for agent work, `lastHead` after a committing step that was not cost-stopped (an unreadable or empty HEAD keeps the old one), `timings` accumulated from exactly two `now()` reads per step, `sink.update` after every step, and a final `sink.step("done", record)`.

One accepted difference: the engine asks `options.costExceeded()` for every `agent` node before the graph's `costStop` checks `hasAgentWork`, where today's `costStop` checks `hasAgentWork` first and the limit last. So `env.costExceeded` is called on agent nodes that have no work. It is a pure read in production (`costLimitReached` over the runtime's cost) and in the test harness, and no G0 trace records it, so the extra calls are unobservable.

`runFeatureMachine` keeps its name, its signature and its module, so every caller and every existing test reaches the ported code unchanged, including `recordFeatureTrace` (`test/helpers/workflow-trace.ts`), which replays the G0 goldens through it.

### File layout

`feature-machine.ts` splits into three files, each under the 600-line limit:

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `src/workflow/feature-machine.ts` | `FeatureSteps`, `FeatureSink`, `FeatureFacts`, `FeatureEnv`, the `FeatureLimits` re-export, `_featureMachineDeps`, and `runFeatureMachine` (the wiring below). |
| `src/workflow/feature-steps.ts` (new) | The eight step functions and their helpers, moved from `feature-machine.ts` (`limitsOf`, `DEFAULT_LIMITS`, `costExceeded`, `assign`, `featureStep`, `NO_MIRROR` and the rest), plus `readHeadSoft`. It exports the step functions, `readHeadSoft`, and the helpers `feature-graph.ts` needs (`featureStep`, `NO_MIRROR`, `isFollowUpRound`, `roundTargets`, `fixNowMinors`). Imports from `feature-machine.ts` are type-only. |
| `src/workflow/feature-graph.ts` (new) | `FEATURE_GRAPH`, and the graph's `costStop` with its `hasAgentWork` check. |

Import direction: `feature-machine.ts` -> `feature-graph.ts` -> `feature-steps.ts` (values), and `feature-steps.ts` -> `feature-machine.ts` (types only, so no runtime cycle for `check:import-cycles`). The workflow imports the engine through its barrel, `@/step-graph`. `FEATURE_GRAPH` is declared with an explicit type, `export const FEATURE_GRAPH: StepGraph<WorkflowFeatureRecord, FeatureEnv, FeatureStep> = defineStepGraph({ ... })`. `defineStepGraph` returns its argument's own type, so without the annotation `kind` and `start` widen to `string` and `runStepGraph` no longer fits the `RunFeatureGraph` type below. Because the annotation makes `nodes` a `Partial` record and `costStop` optional, tests reach them with `FEATURE_GRAPH.costStop?.(...)` and a small node accessor that throws on a missing node, never a non-null `!` (a biome error) or a cast. The step functions keep their current names (`repoGatesStep`, `branchReviewStep`, `branchFixStep`, `branchReReviewStep`, `adjudicateStep`, `finalGatesStep`, `gateRepairStep`, `publishStep`).

### Node table

`FEATURE_GRAPH`: `start` `"repo-gates"`, `end` `["done"]`, `costStopProduces` `["costLimited"]`. No node declares `needs` and the graph declares no `inputs` (see Out of Scope).

| Node | `kind` | `commits` | `produces` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo-gates` | `gate` | no | `repoGates`, `gateFindings`, `nextFindingId` |
| `branch-review` | `agent` | no | `reviewRan`, `cannotVerify`, `reviewUnread`, `reviewOpen`, `nextFindingId`, `minors`, `newMinors` |
| `branch-fix` | `agent` | yes | `fixBase`, `fixRan`, `fixRounds` |
| `branch-rereview` | `agent` | no | `reReviewSkipped`, `reviewOpen`, `nextFindingId`, `minors`, `newMinors`, `fixTargets` |
| `adjudicate` | `agent` | no | `rulings` |
| `final-gates` | `gate` | no | `finalGates`, `finalGateFindings`, `gateRepairFindings` |
| `gate-repair` | `agent` | yes | `gateRepairRounds` |
| `publish` | `forge` | yes | `outcome`, `ci`, `reasons`, `url`, `approval`, `ciDetail`, `storyStates`, `head`, `passed`, `flaggedDecisions`, `endedAt` |

The agent nodes are exactly today's `AGENT_STEPS` and the committing nodes are exactly today's `COMMIT_STEPS`. Each `produces` list is every key the step function's patches can name today, other than `step`, including the keys a patch states as `undefined` to clear them (`fixTargets`, `gateRepairFindings`, `approval`, `ciDetail`).

### Transitions

A node with one destination declares no `exits` and one unconditional transition. A node that branches declares the exit labels below and returns exactly one of them on every path; its transitions are one `{ on, to }` per label, in this order.

| Node | Exit | Returned when (today's code path) | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo-gates` | — | always | `branch-review` |
| `branch-review` | — | always (reviewed, no seed, or review not run) | `branch-fix` |
| `branch-fix` | `nothing-to-fix` | the round has no item to fix | `branch-rereview` |
| `branch-fix` | `capped` | the round is past `maxBranchFixRounds` | `adjudicate` |
| `branch-fix` | `no-base` | the fix base HEAD could not be read | `adjudicate` |
| `branch-fix` | `fixed` | the fix session ran, failed or not | `branch-rereview` |
| `branch-rereview` | `nothing-to-check` | no item to re-review, or no `fixBase` | `adjudicate` |
| `branch-rereview` | `skipped` | the re-review did not run | `adjudicate` |
| `branch-rereview` | `again` | the next round has targets | `branch-fix` |
| `branch-rereview` | `settled` | the re-review ran and no round follows | `adjudicate` |
| `adjudicate` | — | always | `final-gates` |
| `final-gates` | `reused` | no fix ran, so the repo gates are reused | `publish` |
| `final-gates` | `green` | the final gate run is green | `publish` |
| `final-gates` | `repair` | red, with findings, and a repair is allowed | `gate-repair` |
| `final-gates` | `red` | red with no repair | `publish` |
| `gate-repair` | — | always (repaired, capped, or nothing to repair) | `final-gates` |
| `publish` | — | always | `done` |

### Cost stop

`FEATURE_GRAPH.costStop(node, record, env)` replaces `costStop` in `feature-machine.ts`. The engine calls it only for an `agent` node while `options.costExceeded()` returns true, so it no longer checks the limit itself. It returns `undefined` when the node has no agent work (`hasAgentWork`, unchanged: the same emptiness checks each step makes first). Otherwise it writes the same skipped line on stage `workflow` (`startStep(FEATURE_SCOPE, node, { announce: false })` then `done("skipped (cost limit reached)")`), the same ledger note `cost limit reached: <node> skipped` with `{ mirror: false }`, and returns `{ patch: { costLimited: true }, to: "final-gates" }`.

`finalGatesStep`'s own check (`gateRepairAllowed` reads `env.costExceeded`) is part of the step body and stays as it is.

### Wiring `runFeatureMachine`

```ts
// src/workflow/feature-machine.ts
/** The engine call, typed for this graph so a test can stub it without a cast. */
type RunFeatureGraph = (
  graph: typeof FEATURE_GRAPH,
  env: FeatureEnv,
  record: WorkflowFeatureRecord,
  hooks: StepGraphHooks<WorkflowFeatureRecord, FeatureStep>,
  options: StepGraphRunOptions<FeatureStep>,
) => Promise<WorkflowFeatureRecord>;

export const _featureMachineDeps: { runStepGraph: RunFeatureGraph } = { runStepGraph };

export function runFeatureMachine(env: FeatureEnv): Promise<WorkflowFeatureRecord> {
  return _featureMachineDeps.runStepGraph(
    FEATURE_GRAPH,
    env,
    env.record,
    { persist: (record) => env.sink.update(record), onStep: (step, record) => env.sink.step(step, record) },
    {
      aborted: () => env.aborted(),
      now: () => env.now(),
      costExceeded: () => env.costExceeded?.() === true,
      readHead: () => readHeadSoft(env),
      onAbort: (step) =>
        new NaxError("Run aborted during the feature workflow", "WORKFLOW_ABORTED", {
          stage: "workflow",
          storyId: "_run",
          step,
        }),
    },
  );
}
```

`logScope` stays unset: the step functions write their own `workflow` lines, which the G0 goldens pin, and the engine then logs nothing. `readHeadSoft` (moved unchanged) catches a failed HEAD read, logs the existing `warn` on stage `workflow` (`Could not read HEAD after a committing step; the record keeps the last one`, `storyId` `_run`) and resolves `undefined`, so the engine's own `step-graph` warning never fires. The shape above is the target; helper names other than the ones it uses are the builder's.

### Integration

Symbols this feature changes. Each **Baseline** exists only to locate today's code and is never the interface to implement; implement the **Target**.

- `runFeatureMachine` in `src/workflow/feature-machine.ts`.
  - Baseline: `async function runFeatureMachine(env: FeatureEnv): Promise<WorkflowFeatureRecord>`, a `for (;;)` loop over the `STEPS` table with `applyPatch`, `costStop`, `COMMIT_STEPS` and `readHeadSoft`.
  - Target: same signature; the body is the one `_featureMachineDeps.runStepGraph(...)` call above.
- The eight step functions.
  - Baseline: `type StepFn = (env: FeatureEnv, rec: WorkflowFeatureRecord) => Promise<Patch>`, in `feature-machine.ts`, each patch naming `step`.
  - Target: `(env: FeatureEnv, rec: WorkflowFeatureRecord) => Promise<StepResult<WorkflowFeatureRecord>>`, in `feature-steps.ts`; no patch names `step`, and a branching step returns its exit label.
- The cost stop.
  - Baseline: `costStop(env, rec, step): Promise<Patch | undefined>`, which checks `AGENT_STEPS`, `hasAgentWork` and `env.costExceeded`, and returns `{ costLimited: true, step: "final-gates" }`.
  - Target: `FEATURE_GRAPH.costStop(node, rec, env): Promise<CostStop<WorkflowFeatureRecord, FeatureStep> | undefined>`, which checks `hasAgentWork` only and returns `{ patch: { costLimited: true }, to: "final-gates" }`.
- Removed from `feature-machine.ts` with nothing in their place: `applyPatch`, `STEPS`, `COMMIT_STEPS`, `AGENT_STEPS`, `StepFn` and the old `costStop` (the engine and `FEATURE_GRAPH` own these now).

Symbols read and not changed (verified on `main` @ `61c6419d2`):

- `runStepGraph`, `defineStepGraph`, `validateStepGraph`, and the types `StepGraph`, `StepResult`, `CostStop`, `StepGraphHooks`, `StepGraphRunOptions` — `@/step-graph`.
- `FeatureEnv`, `FeatureSteps`, `FeatureSink`, `FeatureFacts` — `src/workflow/feature-machine.ts` (stay there, unchanged).
- `WorkflowFeatureRecord`, `FeatureStep` — `src/workflow/types.ts`.
- `startStep`, `describeFindings` — `src/workflow/run-log.ts`; `ledgerText` — `src/workflow/ledger.ts`.
- `buildFeatureEnv` — `src/workflow/feature-env.ts`; `runWorkflowFeature` — `src/workflow/feature.ts` (calls `runFeatureMachine` through `_featureRunDeps`; both unchanged).
- `recordFeatureTrace`, `compareWithGolden` — `test/helpers/workflow-trace.ts`; `makeFeatureMachineHarness`, `featureMachineFixtures` — `test/helpers/workflow-feature-machine.ts`.

### Equivalence evidence

The port is correct when today's tests pass without a single edit. In particular:

- `test/unit/workflow/feature-machine-equivalence.test.ts` replays all G0 feature scenarios through `runFeatureMachine` and compares them with the committed goldens in `test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/feature/`.
- `feature-machine.test.ts`, `feature-machine-fix-rounds.test.ts` (round caps, a lowered cap on resume, the gate-repair cap), `feature-machine-cost.test.ts`, `feature-machine-honesty.test.ts`, `feature-machine-log.test.ts`, `feature-machine-publish-record.test.ts`, `feature-events.test.ts` and `feature-flagged-decisions.test.ts` cover the paths the goldens do not.

None of those files and no golden changes (see `### Modifies`). A difference in any of them is a behaviour change and a defect in the port, never a fixture to refresh.

### Failure Handling

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Abort observed before a step | Rejects with `NaxError` `WORKFLOW_ABORTED`, message `Run aborted during the feature workflow`, context `{ stage: "workflow", storyId: "_run", step }`; the step does not run (as today). |
| The record's `step` is not a feature step | Rejects with `NaxError` `STEP_GRAPH_UNKNOWN_NODE` before any seam call. Today the loop fails with a `TypeError` on the missing `STEPS` entry, and only after the abort check; no valid record reaches this path. |
| A step function throws | The error propagates unchanged and the last persisted record still names that step (as today). |
| A step patches a key its node does not declare | Rejects with `STEP_GRAPH_UNDECLARED_OUTPUT`. This is a programming error the node table rules out; the existing suites exercise every patch. |
| HEAD cannot be read after a committing step | `readHeadSoft` logs its existing `warn` on stage `workflow`, the record keeps the previous `lastHead`, and the run continues (as today). |

**Scope** — In: modify only `packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts`; create `packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-steps.ts`, `packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-graph.ts`, `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-graph.test.ts`, and `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-machine-graph.test.ts`. The machine file keeps the public interfaces and FeatureLimits re-export. The new graph tests cover declarations and costStop; the new machine-graph tests cover dependency wiring and actual-engine failure paths. All paths above under src/ and test/ are relative to packages/nax. Out: there is no other story in this PRD; the adjacent feature boundaries below remain excluded.

- Changing the step graph engine (`src/step-graph/`): G2 consumes it as G1 shipped it.
- Editing any existing test file or any golden under `test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/`, or regenerating goldens with `NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1`: the unchanged suites are the equivalence evidence.
- Changing `buildFeatureEnv` (`src/workflow/feature-env.ts`) or `runWorkflowFeature` (`src/workflow/feature.ts`): the `FeatureEnv` seams stay exactly as they are.
- The story workflow (`src/workflow/story-loop.ts`, `runStoryLoop`, `workflowStage`): G3 ports it.
- Declaring `needs` on the feature nodes and `inputs` on the graph: what each step reads is settled in G4, when steps take a narrow step context instead of the whole record and `FeatureEnv`.
- A narrow step context, a PR context, and running any feature step outside a nax run: G4.
- Setting `logScope` for the feature graph, or any new log line, ledger line, artifact, record field or record key order: the port is behaviour-identical.
- The live-run check the master plan requires for G2 (one real `nax run` on the new build matching the old build): a manual step after merge, run only with the user's approval, not story work.

**Interface** — The Wiring block above is the verbatim target implementation and typed test seam. The step functions' target signature is `(env: FeatureEnv, rec: WorkflowFeatureRecord) => Promise<StepResult<WorkflowFeatureRecord>>`; FEATURE_GRAPH's explicit declaration and costStop signature are given above. Public FeatureEnv, FeatureSteps, FeatureSink, FeatureFacts, WorkflowFeatureRecord, and FeatureStep remain unchanged.

**Implementation and test strategy notes** — Use tdd-simple: write failing assertions in the two new test modules using bun:test and the existing harness, then implement this mechanical extraction and graph wiring. For wiring assertions, save `_featureMachineDeps.runStepGraph`, install a fully typed spy that captures graph/env/record/hooks/options and resolves to record R, and restore it after every test, as hooks-workflow.test.ts restores _featureRunDeps. Exercise hooks and options via those captured arguments. Use a controlled clock spy to assert the value returned by the same env.now invocation: the harness clock increments on every call, so comparing against a second env.now call would be incorrect. For cost-stop ledger assertions, provide a local sink.ledger spy recording both arguments; do not alter the text-only harness. Use a fresh harness record with one important reviewOpen finding for the branch-fix cost-stop assertions so follow-up-round targeting does not suppress that work. For actual-engine tests restore the real dependency before running the harness. Include the specified unknown cursor, no-base HEAD failure, resumed round-2 HEAD failure, and failure-table cases. Capture all logger stages in the new tests that assert no step-graph entries: recordFeatureTrace intentionally filters to workflow and cannot prove their absence. For the programming-error case, run a test-local copy of FEATURE_GRAPH with a copied node whose run returns an undeclared output; do not mutate the shared FEATURE_GRAPH, modify the engine, or add a production injection seam. The copied graph retains the original produces declarations so the existing engine performs the rejection. Preserve every existing test and golden unchanged. Verification note: the removals are checked by the build and static gates (`bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:all`, which runs `check:file-sizes` and `check:import-cycles`), and the existing suites listed in Design § Equivalence evidence pass unchanged. `bun run test:coverage` covers the two new source files. This verification is part of implementation, not another story or acceptance criterion.

[unit] When a feature node returns a patch containing a key absent from its declared produces, the graph run rejects with a NaxError whose code is "STEP_GRAPH_UNDECLARED_OUTPUT"; this is a programming error the node table rules out.

routing.reasoning: This five-file change mechanically extracts existing step bodies and wires a fully specified graph to the shipped engine through the established typed _deps pattern, with no new abstraction, dependency or public contract; tdd-simple uses the two new test modules plus unchanged golden traces to protect transition, callback, resume and HEAD-read behavior.

modifiedFiles.reason: the step functions, `readHeadSoft` and their helpers move to the new steps module (see Creates); `applyPatch`, `STEPS`, `COMMIT_STEPS`, `AGENT_STEPS`, `StepFn` and the old `costStop` are deleted; the file keeps `FeatureSteps`, `FeatureSink`, `FeatureFacts`, `FeatureEnv`, the `FeatureLimits` re-export, and `runFeatureMachine`, whose body becomes the `_featureMachineDeps.runStepGraph` call of Design § Wiring.

analysis:
This is a mechanical refactor of the existing feature workflow in @nathapp/nax, not a greenfield workflow or a new engine. Codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable, so discovery used direct source reads and text searches. The binding scope is exactly US-001, workdir packages/nax, with no dependencies. Only packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts is modified; four new files are created. No package manifests, callers, existing tests, test helpers, goldens, engine files, or other packages need changes.

Baseline and impact: packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-machine.ts:39 defines FeatureSteps; :58 defines FeatureSink; :66 defines FeatureFacts; :72 defines FeatureEnv; :85 re-exports FeatureLimits. Keep these public interfaces in that module unchanged. The current module is 592 lines, leaving almost no room under the 600-line hard source limit documented in docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md. Its private Patch/StepFn and applyPatch are at feature-machine.ts:93-113. The eight implementations begin at :182 (repoGatesStep), :212 (branchReviewStep), :251 (branchFixStep), :312 (branchReReviewStep), :371 (adjudicateStep), :376 (finalGatesStep), :409 (gateRepairStep), and :472 (publishStep). Move those implementations and their helpers into feature-steps.ts, preserving seam calls, artifacts, ledger writes, workflow-stage startStep lines, optional spreads, key order, wall-clock reads, and all branch-round logic. Only wrap the patches in StepResult and replace cursor outputs with exit labels. Keep undefined-valued output keys explicit: applyPatch currently deletes them, notably fixTargets, gateRepairFindings, approval, and ciDetail. The helpers needed by feature-graph.ts must be exported. Move readHeadSoft unchanged from feature-machine.ts:460. Move hasAgentWork (:521) and the cost-stop behavior (:542) into feature-graph.ts, but remove the limit and agent-set checks there because the engine owns them. Delete applyPatch, StepFn, STEPS (:552), AGENT_STEPS (:509), COMMIT_STEPS (:550), and the old loop (:563 onward); do not leave parallel orchestration policies behind.

Callers and compatibility: packages/nax/src/workflow/feature.ts:15 imports runFeatureMachine and :41 exposes it through _featureRunDeps. Its resume policy compares lastHead ?? startHead at :129 and resumes transient drafts directly at publish at :155, so retaining old lastHead on an unreadable or empty HEAD and clearing stale publish facts are essential. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-env.ts:10 imports FeatureEnv/FeatureSink/FeatureSteps; :35 builds the production env, :91 supplies its sink, and :114 supplies the pure runtime costLimitReached check. packages/nax/src/workflow/step-model.ts:16 imports FeatureSteps as a type. All stay unchanged. The dependency direction must be feature-machine -> feature-graph -> feature-steps for values; feature-steps imports FeatureEnv from feature-machine only as a type. Workflow imports the existing engine barrel @/step-graph, whose exports are at packages/nax/src/step-graph/index.ts:14-30. Explicitly annotate FEATURE_GRAPH as StepGraph<WorkflowFeatureRecord, FeatureEnv, FeatureStep>; defineStepGraph preserves its argument type rather than imposing that type. Optional costStop and Partial nodes mean tests use optional invocation and a checked accessor instead of casts or non-null assertions.

Existing engine contracts and migration: packages/nax/src/step-graph/types.ts:29 declares ENGINE_KEYS as step, timings, and lastHead; :31 defines StepResult, :46 defines StepNode, :67 defines StepGraph, and :88 defines StepGraphRunOptions. Nodes must declare every possible patch key, including undefined-valued clears, and may never patch engine keys. No node needs and no graph inputs are added in G2. The engine already supplies all loop policies: packages/nax/src/step-graph/run.ts:42 rejects unknown nodes; :68 rejects undeclared outputs; :150 applies undefined-as-delete patches; :207 reads committing HEAD fail-soft; :232 restricts cost-stop handling to agent nodes; :262 executes nodes and transitions before the committing HEAD read; :283 runs lookup, abort, onStep, first clock read, cost stop, result, second clock read, persistence; :302 persists the next record; :323 emits the final end hook. Its logScope-controlled logging is at :193, so omit logScope entirely. The injected readHeadSoft must catch HEAD failures itself so the engine's fallback step-graph warning is never emitted. publishStep still reads HEAD for its own head output and the engine still reads it again for lastHead, matching the old loop. A committing node is marked commits even on an early-return path; do not introduce a work-ran optimization that changes HEAD read ordering. validateStepGraph is declaration-only at packages/nax/src/step-graph/validate.ts:108; defineStepGraph at :131 returns the same graph when validation succeeds. The one sanctioned invalid-record change is STEP_GRAPH_UNKNOWN_NODE before abort or seam calls instead of the old missing-table TypeError. The extra costExceeded reads on agent nodes with no work are allowed because the check is pure; no-work cost stops must still return undefined. All other observable behavior stays identical.

Evidence and test design: packages/nax/test/helpers/workflow-feature-machine.ts:67 supplies makeFeatureMachineHarness; :80 provides scripted steps; :129 provides the sink; :150 returns captured calls, updates, ledger texts, and artifacts. Its ledger captures text only (:133), so new graph cost-stop tests need a local ledger spy that captures both text and options, without editing this helper. The helpers are exported through packages/nax/test/helpers/index.ts:164-165. packages/nax/test/helpers/workflow-trace.ts:167 wraps every available FeatureSteps seam; :187 wraps sink writes; :217 runs the real runFeatureMachine and records both successful and thrown outcomes. The log collector at :226-227 filters to workflow, which is why the new tests must explicitly check that there are no step-graph-stage entries. The committed feature golden directory contains clean, one/two-fix-round, residual, red repo gates, gate repair, skipped review/rereview, empty seed, unreadable HEAD, cost stop, abort, resume, publication, failed-fix, minor-triage, and quality-floor scenarios. packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-machine-equivalence.test.ts:89 onward drives these through the same entry point, not a stub. Never refresh goldens or change existing assertions to accept drift. Existing feature-machine.test.ts, feature-machine-fix-rounds.test.ts, feature-machine-cost.test.ts, feature-machine-honesty.test.ts, feature-machine-log.test.ts, feature-machine-publish-record.test.ts, feature-events.test.ts, feature-flagged-decisions.test.ts, feature.test.ts, and step-models-log.test.ts also depend on the unchanged entry point. packages/nax/test/unit/pipeline/subscribers/hooks-workflow.test.ts:35-39 demonstrates saving and restoring a mutable dependency object after each test; use the same discipline for _featureMachineDeps.

Implementation sequence within the single story: write new graph-data/cost-stop and dependency-wiring tests first, including actual-engine unknown-cursor and HEAD-failure scenarios; extract the unchanged step bodies into feature-steps.ts while changing their return envelope and exits; declare FEATURE_GRAPH with exact node metadata, outputs and ordered transitions; replace the loop with the specified typed _featureMachineDeps.runStepGraph call; then use unchanged real-engine equivalence tests as the regression oracle. This is an internal in-place port with no record migration, feature flag, alternate runner, new configuration, or caller migration. Main risks are an omitted declared key on a rare path, an exit that no transition matches, changed round-cap or lowered-cap resume behavior, changed order of ledger/log/artifact writes, mishandled undefined clears, duplicate/missing HEAD reads, an accidental runtime import cycle, a leaked dependency stub between tests, or added engine-stage logs invisible to the golden collector. New tests belong only in feature-graph.test.ts and feature-machine-graph.test.ts. Use bun:test and the existing helpers. From packages/nax, targeted tests should include both new files, unchanged workflow suites, and hooks-workflow.test.ts; never run bare bun test or bun run nax. Verification includes bun run typecheck, bun run check:all (including file sizes and import cycles), the unchanged suites, and a manual bun run test:coverage because coverage is not part of the normal pipeline. Do not turn those gates into acceptance criteria or create a validation-only story. The real old/new-build nax run comparison is a user-approved manual post-merge activity, not implementation work.

Refine-pass audit against the spec (acceptanceCriteria indices below are 1-based within US-001): spec AC-1 is preserved in criteria 1-3 (import path, validation result, start and end); AC-2 in 4-5 (all eight kinds and exact agent set); AC-3 in 6 (exact committing set); AC-4 in 7-8 (all output sets and costStopProduces); AC-5 in 9-10 (ordered transition pairs including absent on, and exit sets including absent exits); AC-6 in 11-12 (branch-fix stop result and exact single ledger call, retaining the own-spy requirement because the harness keeps text only); AC-7 in 13-16 (empty adjudication and null-seed review each return undefined and write nothing); AC-8 in 17-18 (typed restored runner spy, first three argument identities and result R, retaining the hooks-workflow restoration comparison); AC-9 in 19-20 (persist/update and onStep/step forwarding); AC-10 in 21-25 (abort and clock forwarding, absent/present cost predicate values, no logScope); AC-11 in 26 (exact onAbort error type, code, message and context); AC-12 in 27-28 (soft HEAD result and the one existing workflow warning with exact message and storyId); AC-13 in 29-31 (bogus cursor cast, UNKNOWN_NODE, no steps or sink calls); AC-14 in 32-36 (one important review finding, always-failing HEAD, done/no fix/no-base ledger/workflow-only warnings/no engine log); AC-15 in 37-40 (all resumed-record fields, default limits with maxBranchFixRounds 2, one fix retaining the round-2 base-reuse qualifier, done, every persisted lastHead h0, no engine log). No spec AC or regression qualifier was dropped. All five failure-table rows are covered: actual abort in 41-42, unknown node in 29-31, unchanged thrown error and persisted cursor in 43-44, undeclared output in 45, and continued operation with the previous lastHead and workflow warning in 27-28 and 35-40. These assertions are observable through returned values, captured callback arguments, thrown errors, records and logs; no quality-gate or test-count assertion is added.

All eleven feature exclusions remain separate and verbatim in outOfScope: story workflow; needs/inputs; narrow/PR contexts and standalone steps; logScope and any new observable artifacts or ordering; env builder and production caller changes; existing tests and golden updates; engine changes; deprecated finish/pipeline; bot review/fix; the user-approved live run; and release/docs. Adjacent exclusions are echoed in the description. The spec has no story-local deferral block. The five contextFiles exactly match the spec's Context Files list and already exist; all four expectedFiles match Creates and none appears in contextFiles. The sole story id, workdir and empty dependencies are retained as bound. Scope includes the extraction, graph, production entry-point wiring and both new tests without authorizing changes to the protected suites or helper. No description/criterion contradiction was found. The initial routing overstated the architectural novelty: source inspection confirms a fully specified five-file mechanical integration with a shipped engine and existing test seams, so medium/tdd-simple is the lightest realistic choice. Clock forwarding wording now identifies the value from the same env.now invocation rather than encouraging an invalid comparison to the harness's next ticking read; transition assertions explicitly project ordered on/to pairs. New test notes explain full-stage logging capture and a test-local copied graph for the undeclared-output negative path without mutating the production graph or expanding scope.
outOfScope: The story workflow (`src/workflow/story-loop.ts`, `runStoryLoop`, `workflowStage`): G3 ports it.
Declaring `needs` on the feature nodes and `inputs` on the graph: what each step reads is settled in G4, when steps take a narrow step context instead of the whole record and `FeatureEnv`.
A narrow step context, a PR context, and running any feature step outside a nax run: G4.
Setting `logScope` for the feature graph, or any new log line, ledger line, artifact, record field or record key order: the port is behaviour-identical.
Changing `buildFeatureEnv` (`src/workflow/feature-env.ts`) or `runWorkflowFeature` (`src/workflow/feature.ts`): the `FeatureEnv` seams stay exactly as they are.

Editing any existing test file or any golden under `test/fixtures/workflow-equivalence/`, or regenerating goldens with `NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1`: the unchanged suites are the equivalence evidence.
Changing the step graph engine (`src/step-graph/`): G2 consumes it as G1 shipped it.
The deprecated `src/finish/` phase and pipeline mode: pipeline mode is frozen.
`nax bot review` and `nax bot fix`: B2 and B3.
The live-run check the master plan requires for G2 (one real `nax run` on the new build matching the old build): a manual step after merge, run only with the user's approval, not story work.
Release notes, user docs and a release: the port has no user-visible surface.
